objective: Build a simple responsive React Todo web app with task creation, deletion, completion toggling, localStorage persistence, unit tests, and a successful production build.
assumptions: Inspect the existing repository before implementation; reuse its package manager, React tooling, language, and test conventions.
If no application exists, initialize a minimal React app with Vite and use Vitest, React Testing Library, and jsdom for tests.
Tasks contain an id, text, and completed boolean.
Completion can be toggled in either direction; task editing, filtering, accounts, and backend services are outside scope.
requirements: Add tasks through a labeled text input and submit button; support Enter submission.
Trim task text and reject empty or whitespace-only submissions.
Toggle individual tasks between active and completed.
Persist task additions, deletions, and completion changes in localStorage and restore them on reload.
Provide a basic responsive, keyboard-accessible interface with distinguishable completed tasks.
Include automated unit tests for task behavior and persistence.
Ensure npm run build completes successfully.
architecture: App owns task state, coordinates task operations, and renders the form, empty state, and task list.
TaskForm owns the input value and invokes an add callback for valid submissions.
TaskItem renders task text, a labeled completion checkbox, and an accessible delete button.
A small storage module encapsulates the storage key, JSON serialization, validation, and exception handling.

Use an illustrative structure of src/App.jsx, src/components/TaskForm.jsx, src/components/TaskItem.jsx, src/storage.js, src/styles.css, and colocated test files; adapt extensions and locations to repository conventions.
Initialize task state lazily from storage, update state immutably, and persist the initialized state whenever tasks change.
implementation_steps: Inspect package.json, source files, repository instructions, and existing tests. Identify reusable tooling and establish the current build and test commands.
Set up only missing React and test infrastructure. Provide build and noninteractive test scripts in package.json.

Implement storage loading and saving under a namespaced key such as todo-app.tasks.v1. Require an array of records with unique nonempty string ids, nonblank string text, and boolean completed values. Return an empty list for missing, malformed, or invalid stored data; catch storage access failures.

Implement App state with lazy storage initialization. Generate a stable unique id when creating each task, append new tasks as incomplete, delete by id, and toggle completion by id using functional state updates.
Implement TaskForm with a visible label, submission handling, whitespace validation, and input clearing after successful addition.
Implement the semantic task list and TaskItem controls, including checkbox state, completed styling, accessible delete labels, and a friendly empty state.
Add minimal responsive CSS with a centered maximum-width container, flexible controls, wrapping long task text, visible focus states, and usable mobile spacing.
Write storage and component tests using isolated localStorage state and realistic user interactions.
Run the complete test suite and npm run build, resolve failures, and manually verify responsive behavior and persistence in the running app.
edge_cases: Empty or whitespace-only submissions create no task.
Duplicate task text is allowed; unique ids ensure independent deletion and completion.
Long task text wraps without horizontal overflow or obscuring controls.
Deleting the final task displays the empty state and persists an empty array.
Missing, malformed, or structurally invalid stored data does not crash the app.
Blocked localStorage or quota failures leave the app usable in memory, although persistence is unavailable.
Existing saved tasks are loaded before persistence runs, preventing initial empty state from overwriting them.
Task text containing HTML-like content is displayed as ordinary text through React rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting valid text by button or Enter adds exactly one incomplete task, trims its text, and clears the input.
Invalid empty submissions leave the task list unchanged.
Deleting a task removes only the selected task.
Toggling a checkbox updates only the selected task and allows it to return to active status.
Reloading restores task text, ordering, and completion states after additions, deletions, and toggles.
Storage failures and invalid saved data produce no uncaught application errors.
The interface remains usable at 320px mobile width and desktop widths without horizontal overflow.
Users can add, toggle, and delete tasks using a keyboard, with accessible labels and visible focus indicators.
Automated tests pass through the configured noninteractive npm test command.
npm run build exits with code 0 and generates the production output.
verification_plan: Test storage loading with missing data, a valid task array, malformed JSON, invalid records, and duplicate ids.
Test storage serialization and ensure read or write exceptions are handled without crashing.
Test initial empty state, button submission, Enter submission, trimming, input clearing, and rejection of blank text.
Test independent completion toggling and deletion, including tasks with identical text and deletion of the final task.
Seed localStorage before rendering and verify hydration; perform each mutation and verify the serialized state, then unmount and remount to confirm restoration.
Clear localStorage and reset mocks between tests to prevent order-dependent results.
Run npm test in noninteractive mode and npm run build from the project root.
Manually inspect the running app at 320px, 768px, and desktop widths, including long text, keyboard navigation, and a browser reload after each task operation.
risks: Existing tooling may differ from the assumed scaffold; preserve working conventions and avoid unnecessary dependency or configuration changes.
localStorage is browser- and origin-specific and may be unavailable; this implementation provides no cross-device synchronization or persistence guarantee when storage fails.
Concurrent edits in multiple browser tabs can overwrite saved state; cross-tab synchronization is outside the requested scope.
jsdom does not validate actual responsive layout, so browser inspection remains necessary alongside unit tests.
